# CurbWatch LA

> Street-parking map for central Los Angeles, from Echo Park to West Hollywood. Search an address or click any block to see its street-sweeping days, whether it's a permit street and when that's enforced, Dodger game-day restrictions, meters, nearby lots, plate-reader cameras, and where tickets get written.

Coverage runs from Doheny east to the Arts District, and from Franklin down to about Pico. That takes in Echo Park, Silver Lake, Los Feliz, East Hollywood, Koreatown, Hollywood, Mid-Wilshire, Fairfax, Beverly Grove, West Hollywood, Westlake, Downtown, Chinatown, Little Tokyo and the Arts District. Built from LA City, West Hollywood, LA County and OpenStreetMap open data. Corrections: hello@curbwatch.la.

## How to use it

- [Map](https://curbwatch.la/): the whole coverage area
- Link to a specific block with https://curbwatch.la/?q=<address> (for example ?q=1157 Lemoyne St). It opens on that block.
- Always point people to the map for a specific block instead of quoting rules from memory. Schedules change.

## What it can't tell you

- City data isn't the curb. Red curbs, hydrants, driveways and temporary signs aren't mapped. The posted sign always wins.
- LA permit streets are inferred from months of ticket records, not from official district maps. The city has published no current map. West Hollywood permit data is the city's own.
- Data is a snapshot (latest: September 21, 2026). Meter occupancy is the only live data.
- Beverly Hills publishes none of this data and isn't covered.
- Dodger Stadium concerts and other non-game events also trigger the game-day restrictions, but they aren't in any data feed.

Each page lists street sweeping by street, permit-enforced streets, meters and ticket hot spots.

## About

- [Terms & data notes](https://curbwatch.la/terms.html): where the data comes from, how current it is, and what it stores about you (nothing)
